consensus_summary: A counterfeit covenant community that claims the identity and privileges of God’s people while opposing God, persecuting the faithful, and thereby serving Satan; the Revelation phrase targets those who say they are Jews and are not, routinely linked with the ‘assembly of the wicked’ of Psalm 22:16 as the hostile company around the Messiah.
book_summary: The counterfeit congregation—an edah (covenant-assembly term) that claims covenant standing while gathered against the covenant’s Lord—exemplified by the evil congregation of Numbers, Korah’s company that declared all holy, the assembly enclosing the Messiah at the cross, and those who say they are Jews and are not.
consensus_core_identification: counterfeit covenant assembly claiming to be God’s people while opposing God and the faithful
book_core_identification: counterfeit edah claiming covenant standing while gathered against the covenant’s Lord
boundary_disagreement: None material; both cover the Revelation opponents, the company at the cross, and false claimants generally. The book’s added OT wilderness paradigms (Numbers 14/16) function as illustrative types of the same referent rather than re-drawing boundaries.
rationale: Minimum cores are identical: a false assembly that pretends covenant legitimacy while opposing the Lord. Extra typological detail (edah terminology, Korah, Numbers rebel camp) elaborates the shared referent without replacing it, narrowing cases, or introducing contradiction. Consensus primary meaning and listed alternatives already encompass the same symbolic force.
strongest_objection: Emphasis on Numbers 14/16 and the technical term edah is heavier than in the consensus, which centers Revelation and Psalm 22; a reader could claim this shifts the definitional center of gravity even while preserving the core.
